titles.title: Placement controls > records the config-popover-flip transient departure and compares the settled box
titles.intent: This case puts a popover at the right edge with `data-bs-popper-config` turning flip off. Bootstrap's popover first renders 4 px low (initial y 269) and settles after one `update` (y 265). The case proves that the engine skips that transient and lands within 1 px of the settled box (lines 485-487). It then consumes the `config-popover-flip` row by passing literal box strings to `ledger.compare`, which uses exact string equality with no tolerance.
titles.assertion_153: It fails at the same line :513. The engine reads `Settled (406.8125,265.40625,175.1875,107.1875,582,372.59375)`, x 0.81 px right of its 141 reading; Bootstrap's side reads the same as on 141.
titles.cause: The row pins pixel coordinates measured on a host where the popover is 155.984375 px wide. On this host Bootstrap's own oracle popover is 175.203125 px wide at x 406, so the Bootstrap cell differs before the engine is even read. A popover's width follows its text, and `system-ui` (first in Bootstrap's `--bs-font-sans-serif`) resolves to DejaVu Sans here (`fc-match`). The cause is therefore this host's font metrics, not Chromium's anchor positioning or the Popper tolerance: the y readings (265.40625) match the row under both versions. Record history for the whole set: the set was named on 2026-10-02 (lanes.md:940), which said the failures "come from the cloud host's Chromium 141" without checking each title. The landing rule (lanes.md:47) lets a unit land when its only failures are these titles, so no unit was ever briefed to repair them. B6 (2026-10-06, lanes.md:214-222) found five of the six still fail under 153 and left the rest to the floor ruling D-10.
titles.repair_options: (a) Re-record the row's literal boxes on the arbiter host under the ruled floor; at 153 the engine cell becomes the 153 string quoted earlier. Any host with different fonts then fails the row. (b) Rewrite the row and the case to record readings that don't depend on the host, namely the 4 px transient and the within-1 px settle the case already asserts, instead of coordinates. (c) Pin the popover's geometry in the fixture, with a fixed width or a font the case loads, so every host reads the same box. Loosening a tolerance does not apply, because the compare is string equality. A version gate does not apply, because 141 and 153 fail alike. No engine change is indicated: the engine already lands within 1 px of the settled box. For the floor itself: scaffold `4725e958` (2026-10-06 19:31 UTC, stage-b/user-rulings-2026-10-06.md row 7) records D-10 as ruled 153, which is later than B6 and later than the `host-bound.md` snapshot (taken at veneer `43ca8a0`).

titles.title: Placement controls > measures the perpendicular keyword dimension swap warrant for constructed rules
titles.intent: This case measures the browser, not the engine. It anchors a 120 x 80 px panel `block-start` above a trigger at top 0 and sets `position-try-fallbacks: flip-start`; the panel must then read 80 x 120 px. That swap is the reason the engine compiles perpendicular fallbacks to named rules in a constructed stylesheet (guide § Placement, veneer.md:607).
titles.assertion_141: `expected 120 to be 80` at :693: after `flip-start` the panel keeps its 120 px width.
titles.cause: This is Chromium 141's own behavior: under `flip-start` the panel never reads the swapped box. The case can't tell whether 141 skips the fallback or applies it without swapping sizes. It is the only one of the six whose cause is the Chromium version. No engine code runs in this case, and the population cases that use the engine's constructed rules pass under 141.
titles.repair_options: (a) Version-gate the expectation with `readChromiumMajor()`, the helper the preflight record case uses (tests/integration.test.ts:345), so that 141 is expected to read no swap. (b) Under the D-10 floor of 153 (recorded at scaffold `4725e958`), keep the case as a 153 contract and treat the 141 reading as below the floor; this host's gates then need 153 selected through `PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, because its default browser is 141.0.7390.37. No tolerance or departure row applies, and no engine change is indicated.

titles.title: Placement moving geometry > 'Popover'-'scroll'
titles.intent: Both realms scroll the boundary scroller by 300 px. The engine's popover, placed `bottom`, must then resolve the same side as Bootstrap's Popper oracle and sit within 1 px of Popper's box and arrow on x, y, width, height, right, and bottom.
titles.assertion_141: `expected 1.390625 to be less than or equal to 1`. The box x is 123.609375 against the oracle's 124 (0.39 px off), and the arrow x is 202.609375 against 204 (1.39 px off). The engine's arrow sits 79 px into the box where Popper's sits 80 px.
titles.assertion_153: Same failure with the same values (box 0.390625 px, arrow 1.390625 px).
titles.cause: Popper's boxes sit on whole pixels (oracle x 124, 136, 104), but the engine leaves the panel at its anchored sub-pixel x. `#apply` rounds the translate delta, not the final position (src/browser/Placement.ts:276), so the panel keeps the .609375 fraction. `#arrow` then computes the arrow from that box using the integer `clientWidth` and `Math.round` (`computeArrow`, src/browser/helpers.ts:1290), which lands one whole pixel short at this fraction; 0.39 + 1 = 1.39 exceeds the 1 px tolerance. When the panel lands at .40625 (`'Popover'-'resize'` under 141), the arrow sits at 80 px and the case passes. The tooltip motion cases at .609375 keep their arrow in step (72 px on both sides), so the whole-pixel step depends on the popover's 175.1875 px width, which is itself font-driven on this host. The cause is neither 141's anchor positioning nor the Popper oracle's tolerance alone: 153 reads the same values.
titles.repair_options: (a) Loosen the arrow tolerance at :1062 (and at the population's :461) to allow the one-pixel arrow step on top of the box's sub-pixel offset. (b) Change the engine: snap the anchored panel to device pixels the way Popper rounds its offsets (round the target position rather than the delta at Placement.ts:276), or compute the arrow from the unrounded target as Popper does. Either needs a probe across the population on 141 and 153. (c) Record the arrow's sub-pixel difference as a departure row under the ruled floor. A version gate does not fit, because 141 and 153 read the same 1.390625.

titles.title: Placement moving geometry > 'Popover'-'transform'
titles.intent: This is the same comparison against Popper's oracle, with the boundary wrapper under `transform: translate(12px, 18px)`. Placement, box, and arrow must each be within 1 px.
titles.assertion_141: `expected 1.390625 to be less than or equal to 1`. The box x is 135.609375 against 136 (0.39 px off), and the arrow x is 214.609375 against 216 (1.39 px off), 79 px into the box against Popper's 80 px.
titles.assertion_153: Same failure with the same values.
titles.cause: The cause is the same as in `'Popover'-'scroll'`. The engine keeps the panel's .609375 sub-pixel x (Placement.ts:276 rounds only the delta), and the arrow coordinate, rounded against the integer `clientWidth` (helpers.ts:1290), drops one whole pixel below Popper's, which places its popover on whole pixels. The result reads the same under 141 and 153.
titles.repair_options: These are the same options as for `'Popover'-'scroll'`: (a) loosen the arrow tolerance at :1062; (b) change the engine to snap the panel to device pixels or compute the arrow from the unrounded target; (c) record a departure row for the arrow offset under the ruled floor. A version gate does not fit.

titles.title: consumes every selected departure
titles.intent: Every Placement-family row that `DepartureLedger` selects from the guide's Engine departures table must be consumed by a passing compare whose case title the row names (`ledger.unused` and `ledger.unproven` must both be empty).
titles.assertion_141: `expected [ { ...(6) } ] to deeply equal []`: `ledger.unused` holds the single `config-popover-flip` row.
titles.assertion_153: Same failure, with the same single row.
titles.cause: This failure follows from the config-popover-flip case. `DepartureLedger.compare` marks a row consumed only when its compare returns no differences and no unused rows (tests/setupBrowser.ts:7597-7650). That case's compare fails at :513, so the row stays unused. No other Placement row is unused under either version.
titles.repair_options: Whatever repairs the config-popover-flip case repairs this title too; it has no repair of its own.

titles.title: Tip initialization: popover > projects markup leaves and refuses the tooltip config and sanitizer attributes
titles.intent: The case runs for both profiles. Markup leaves must project (`data-bs-title` as HTML, `data-bs-custom-class`). The tooltip's `data-bs-config` and the sanitizer attributes (`data-bs-sanitize="false"`, `data-bs-allow-list`) must be refused, so the `onerror` image is stripped. The typed `position: { side: 'right' }` must override the markup's `data-bs-placement="bottom"`; `tip.placement` reads the resolved side after layout and flip.
titles.assertion_141: `expected 'top' to be 'right'` at :1166. The earlier checks pass: the `Safe` text, no `[onerror]` element, and the `message` class. The tooltip profile passes.
titles.assertion_153: Same failure (`'top'` where `'right'` is expected); the tooltip profile passes.
titles.cause: The trigger sits at left 150px in Vitest's default 414 px viewport; the case sets no viewport. The population case `Popover-right-center-ltr` uses the same `Anchor` button and body text at the same x, and on this host both Popper's oracle and the engine resolve it to `top`. A 175.2 px popover plus the 8 px offset beside the 82.4 px trigger needs 415.6 px. The engine flips exactly as Bootstrap flips, so the expected side `right` holds only where the popover is narrower: the same font-metric cause as the config-popover-flip row. Neither the Chromium version nor a tolerance is involved, and the sanitizer and config assertions pass.
titles.repair_options: (a) Change the fixture so the configured side fits under any host font, by moving the trigger left or giving this case a wider viewport; the side assertion then reads the typed override rather than the flip. (b) Assert the configured side without the flip's influence, for example with flip turned off in the typed options; this changes what the case proves, so it is a ruling. A version gate, a tolerance, and a departure row do not apply: 141 and 153 fail alike, the assertion compares a side name, and the engine matches Bootstrap. No engine change is indicated.

other_failures_153: Placement population > 'Popover-top-center-ltr' (Placement.test.ts:461, expected 1.390625 to be less than or equal to 1)

Cause shared by all 32, same as the 'Popover'-'scroll' and -'transform' titles: under 153 the popover anchors natively (the engine writes `translate: 0px`, where 141 writes `translate: -16px 201px` for 'Popover-right-center-ltr'). The panel lands at x 103.609375 against Popper's 104 (0.39 px), and the arrow at 79 px into the box against Popper's 80 (1.39 px). Under 141 the panel lands at 103.40625 with the arrow at 80 px (0.59 px), so these titles pass there. All tooltip population and motion titles pass under 153. Tip.test.ts has no 153 failure outside the one host-bound popover title. Total: 37 failed of 357 (141: 6 failed of 357). The guide's sentences that the population cases measure every floating and arrow box within 1 px of Popper's, and that the browser proofs run on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (veneer.md:607-609), don't hold on this host at 153.
